title: feat(components,plugin-grid,types): implement `ListColumn.wrap` — a column that says it wraps now wraps (#6650)
body:
Fixes #6650

Implements the maintainer ruling recorded in [comment 5510087118](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/6650#issuecomment-5510087118) — **Option B, implement**. Not option A: the card body, the 2026-08-28 triage and the 2026-09-02 spec seat all recommended retiring `ListColumn.wrap` from `@objectstack/spec`, and the maintainer took B. Nothing here touches `@objectstack/spec`; the declaration and its `describe('Allow text wrapping')` stay, and the renderer catches up to them.

Verified on head `1664981ee`.

## What lands

1. **`data-table.tsx` reads the key.** A column with `wrap: true` renders its cell body `whitespace-normal break-words` in place of `truncate`. Absent or `false` renders exactly what shipped before.
2. **`ObjectGrid.generateColumns()` forwards it again** — the hop objectui#5453 deleted, back with a reader — spelled `!== undefined` so an explicit `wrap: false` arrives as a decision rather than an absence.
3. **`TableColumn` declares `wrap`**, the zod mirror carries it (a non-strict mirror would otherwise strip an authored key on the parse road), and `StaticTableColumn` tombstones it with remediation text — the same lockstep objectui#6424 / #6425 established.
4. **Two DOM pins replace the pass-through shape**, and two patch changesets.

## ⚠️ Premise correction: the pin the ruling names no longer exists

The ruling says the bridge forward at `list-view.ts:71` "stays and is now a live forward", and that the pin at `packages/react/src/spec-bridge/__tests__/SpecBridge.test.ts:180` is retargeted. **Neither file is on `main`.** `bf283414f` — objectui#6632, 2026-08-29, three days before the ruling — retired the whole spec-bridge: `SpecBridge`, `bridgeListView`, `bridgeFormView`. There is no `packages/react/src/spec-bridge/` directory, and `packages/react` has no column-level `wrap` reference at all.

So `packages/react` is untouched by this PR, and the ruling's clause about it is unexecutable rather than skipped. **The intent behind it is executed in full**, at the place the chain now runs: the pass-through assertion is gone from the repo already, and what replaces it are two pins that assert a rendered cell rather than a forwarded key —

- `packages/components/.../__tests__/data-table-column-wrap.test.tsx` — the renderer's own branches, including the precedence below.
- `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/ObjectGrid.columnWrapForward.test.tsx` — an authored `ListColumn` in an `object-grid` schema, asserted on the DOM at the far end, so it goes red if any link breaks.

This also incidentally confirms the triage's complaint about the old shape: `#6632` demolished the far end of that chain and nothing went red, because nothing had ever asserted the key reached a renderer.

### The pins are proven red, not assumed red

With both consumers reverted to `origin/main` (mutation confirmed on disk against the `HEAD` blob hashes, restored by trap, restore confirmed byte-identical afterwards):

```
Test Files  2 failed (2)
     Tests  5 failed | 5 passed (10)
  × wraps the cell when the column says so
  × the decision is per column, not per table
  × an authored `wrap: true` reaches the DOM as whitespace-normal break-words
  × a non-link column honours the authored key too — both cell shapes, one key
  × a wrapping column and a truncating column coexist in one grid
```

The five that stay green are the controls — `truncate` on absence, on explicit `false`, and the `fitContent` precedence — which assert today's unchanged behaviour and *must* survive the revert.

## The `fitContent` × `wrap` precedence — decided, measured, pinned

The ruling carried this forward as a confidence gap and assigned the decision here. **`fitContent` wins.**

A fit cell is `width: 1%` with `minWidth` and `maxWidth` left undefined, so the auto table layout sizes that column from its content alone. `whitespace-nowrap` is what holds the content's min-content width at its max-content width — one line. Drop nowrap and min-content falls back to the longest *word*. Honouring `wrap` on a fit column therefore does not wrap it, it **collapses** it.

Measured in Chromium 1194 with the cell shape reproduced exactly (900px container, `table-layout: auto`, sibling column at 400px, the same utility classes `data-table` emits):

| fit cell, same content | width | lines | height |
|---|---|---|---|
| `whitespace-nowrap` (today, and what ships) | **463.9px** | 1 | 36.5px |
| `whitespace-normal break-words` (if `wrap` won) | **70.9px** | 10 | 216.5px |

6.5x narrower and 5.9x taller. The author who wrote both keys asked for two incompatible things, and the outcome of yielding to `wrap` is not wrapped text — it is a column squeezed to its longest word, which serves neither key.

⚠️ **What the same measurement does *not* show**, recorded because the obvious argument for this precedence turns out to be the weaker one: the shipped fit producer — `ObjectGrid`'s injected `_actions` column — measures **identically both ways** (179px), because `RowActionMenu` carries its own `whitespace-nowrap` on a nowrap flex row. The collapse is not a risk to the actions column. It is what a *text* column authored with both keys would get, and that is the case the branch refuses.

The same harness confirms the feature does its job on an ordinary column: `truncate` clips (`scrollWidth` 705 against `clientWidth` 576), `whitespace-normal break-words` renders all of it over two lines with nothing clipped.

## A second consumer the ruling could not have known about

The end-to-end pin failed on its first run, reading back `…cursor-pointer truncate block max-w-full` from a column authored `wrap: true`. `ObjectGrid`'s `LinkCell` — the record link that **column one of almost every grid** renders through — wears its own `truncate`, which clamps the text back to one line *inside* a cell body that is willing to wrap. Honouring the key only downstream would have shipped a `wrap` that works on columns 2..N and silently does nothing on column 1: this card's own defect, reproduced one element deeper, in the column most likely to hold long text.

`LinkCell` now takes the authored key. The wrapping variant is **derived** from the pinned class list (`LINK_CELL_CLASS.replace('truncate', …)`) rather than written out, so the two cannot drift and the default markup stays byte-identical — `ObjectGrid.linkCellAnchor.test.tsx` pins that as full markup and is untouched.

Worth noting how this was found: the two "still truncates" controls in that pin were originally passing **for the wrong reason** — they were reading `LinkCell`'s `truncate`, not the key's. They now assert over the whole `<td>`, which no single layer can satisfy while another contradicts it.

## Bytes

Measured with `check:eager-closure` over two real console builds in one container — same `node_modules`, same turbo cache, only the four source files switched between `origin/main` and this branch (mutation and restore both confirmed against `HEAD` blob hashes).

| chunk (gzip) | before | after | delta | headroom |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`framework`** | 523,823 | 523,823 | **+0** | 0.2 KB |
| `ui-components` | 396,598 | 396,625 | **+27** | 2.3 KB |
| `vendor-objectstack` | 948,329 | 948,329 | +0 | 18.2 KB |
| aggregate eager closure | 3,254,604 | 3,254,665 | +61 | 13.0 KB |

**`framework` does not move.** That was the constraint to respect — it has ~0.2 KB of headroom and #7399 parked on it — and the reading is exact zero, not "within noise": the byte counts are identical. `ui-components` takes +27 gzipped against 2.3 KB of headroom. No ceiling raised, no baseline re-pinned, no gate weakened.

```
✅ framework                511.5 KB / 511.7 KB ceiling (headroom 0.2 KB)
✅ ui-components            387.3 KB / 389.6 KB ceiling (headroom 2.3 KB)
```

## Verification

All on `1664981ee`, each command's exit read before any pipe.

- `vitest run packages/types packages/plugin-grid` — **204 files / 2549 tests passed**
- `vitest run packages/components` — **226 files / 2077 tests passed**
- `turbo run type-check` (types, plugin-grid, components) — **16/16 tasks**, and this is where a real regression surfaced: `columnHoldsExpiry-6424.test.ts` used `wrap` as its example of a key *inside* the derived tombstone band, and declaring the key on `TableColumn` removed it from the band by construction. That is a compile-time `Expect<>`, invisible to vitest. The control is repointed to `summary`, a `ListColumn` member no `TableColumn` declares.
- `turbo run lint` — **repo-wide, 47/47 tasks, 0 errors**
- Gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:eager-closure`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:dist-completeness`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:published-tsconfig-exclude`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:spec-floors`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:self-import`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:readme-exports`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:sdui-registration-pins`, `check:element-data-source-declaration` — all green. `check:readme-exports` first failed as **PREREQUISITE NOT MET** (`packages/cli` and `packages/plugin-ai` had no `dist` on disk, neither touched here); it is green after building them.

The `col.<key>` read set of `data-table.tsx` was re-derived rather than inherited — 14 distinct keys, matching the count the `ObjectGrid` docblock claims, with `wrap` now among them.

## Declined, deliberately

- **Header cells do not wrap.** The ruling says a `wrap: true` column "renders its **cells**"; the header keeps its `whitespace-nowrap truncate`. Widening the key to headers would be a second behaviour change with no ruling behind it.
- **No spec change, no retirement, no `needs:contract-review`.** Clause ② is no per the ruling.
- **`packages/react` untouched** — see the premise correction above.
- **No repo-wide `wrap` sweep.** Triage fenced this to the one key; other renderers that clip long text are not in scope and none were found silently promising this key.
